name: Cocina Mi Fonda
description: A shared-table fonda on Calle López that Chilango says has been famous for its saffron paella for more than 70 years. Also serves caldo gallego, fabada, pollo con mole verde and milanesa, with flan and natilla for dessert. Expect around 200 pesos or more per person.
special_quality: Seven decades of Spanish-immigrant paella served at communal tables in the Centro.
google_maps_query: Cocina Mi Fonda, Centro Histórico, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Fonda La Reforma
description: Fonda at Héroes and Degollado in Guerrero whose facade advertises 75 years of tradition; Chilango's 2015 piece says it began as a pancita stand 80+ years ago. Menu is classic comida corrida: mole, chiles rellenos, pancita, chicharrón en salsa verde, enchiladas, from about 70 pesos. Salvador Novo and Octavio Paz are rumored regulars.
special_quality: A trip back in time: pancita-stand-turned-fonda with literary-regular lore, from ~70 pesos.
google_maps_query: Fonda La Reforma, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Fonda La Beatricita
description: Founded in 1907 in the Centro by Doña Beatriz Muciño and in the Zona Rosa since the 1970s. Chilango lists mole poblano, tacos (cecina, carnitas, guisado), pozolito and flan de caramelo. Source article is from 2015, so verify it is still operating.
special_quality: A 1907 family fonda that survived a move into the Zona Rosa.
google_maps_query: Fonda La Beatricita, Juárez, Ciudad de Mexico

name: La Oaxaqueña (Mercado de Portales)
description: Stall inside Mercado de Portales open for over 40 years with about 15 guisados daily, handmade tortillas, fruit waters, pancita and tlayudas, plus breakfast. Around 80 pesos per person per Chilango.
special_quality: Fifteen rotating guisados and handmade tortillas for ~80 pesos in a 40-year-old market stall.
address: Mercado de Portales, Portales (stall location verify)
google_maps_query: La Oaxaqueña (Mercado de Portales), Ciudad de Mexico

name: Los Cazadores
subcategory: Comida corrida, shared table with live music
description: Everyone eats at one large shared table, often with live musicians. Serves meat tortas and pastas on a ~70-peso comida corrida. Chilango suggests coffee at Villarías afterward.
special_quality: One long communal table with roaming musicians for a ~70-peso lunch in the Centro.
google_maps_query: Los Cazadores, Centro Histórico, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Los Tres Reyes
description: Weekend barbacoa institution in Alfonso XIII, served with consomé or michelada at long shared tables where norteña musicians play requests for a fee. Sopitas/Time Out note 70+ years of experience and crowds. Open Saturday and Sunday 8:30 to 17:00 per Chilango.
special_quality: Weekend barbacoa with paid norteña requests at communal tables, 70+ years running.
google_maps_query: Los Tres Reyes, Ciudad de Mexico

name: La Oveja Negra
description: Barbacoa from sheep raised in Hidalgo, prepared in the traditional Hidalgo style using a recipe dating to the 1950s. Staff in green handle tortillas, meat and tables. Open late (to 23:00) unlike most barbacoa spots.
special_quality: Hidalgo barbacoa that stays open until 11 p.m. in a city where barbacoa is a morning affair.
google_maps_query: La Oveja Negra, Santa María la Ribera, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Barbacoa de Santiago
description: Nápoles barbacoa with salsa borracha tacos and take-home kilos packed with avocado and chicharrón. Serves from morning until mid-afternoon, open Mon-Thu 8:00-20:00 and Fri-Sun 8:00-22:00 per Chilango; Time Out also cites its barbacoa flautas.
special_quality: Reliable weekday barbacoa with a famous salsa borracha.
google_maps_query: Barbacoa de Santiago, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Tripolandia
description: Neighborhood taquería since 1955 on Plaza Juan José Baz, known for tripa cooked twice for crisp texture.
special_quality: Tripa tacos fried twice, a Centro fixture since 1955.
address: Plaza Juan José Baz 5, Centro Histórico
google_maps_query: Tripolandia, Centro Histórico, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Yeshua Tacos
description: Offal-focused taquería on Calle del Carmen with over 50 years of history, two salsa options and a loyal Centro crowd.
special_quality: Five decades of vísceras tacos near the Zócalo.
google_maps_query: Yeshua Tacos, Centro Histórico, Ciudad de Mexico

name: El Taco Taco (pavo frito)
description: Chilango calls it an unusual pavería behind the Barrio Chino serving fried turkey in tacos or tortas.
special_quality: A taquería built around fried turkey.
address: Behind Barrio Chino, Centro Histórico (verify exact address)
google_maps_query: El Taco Taco (pavo frito), Centro Histórico, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Huesitos El Güero
description: About 25 years old on Oriente 95 in Mártires de Río Blanco; you order by number of fried pork huesitos with a spicy red salsa.
special_quality: Fried pork-bone tacos ordered by the piece with a fiery red salsa.
google_maps_query: Huesitos El Güero, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Los Provolones
description: Doctores taquería serving charcoal-grilled meats and sausages each topped with melted provolone.
special_quality: Provolone on everything from the charcoal grill.
google_maps_query: Los Provolones, Doctores, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Zacapu
description: Lagunilla neighborhood favorite with a sweet-spicy morita salsa; often sells out early.
special_quality: Achicalada carnitas that vanish by midday.
google_maps_query: Zacapu, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Tacos Domingo
description: Charcoal-grilled asada, chuleta and costilla tacos, volcán, torta árabe and cebollitas; meat also sold by 200g, 500g or 1kg. Food & Pleasure (Dec 2025) recommends it for the historic center.
special_quality: Charcoal meats by the kilo in the Centro.
google_maps_query: Tacos Domingo, Centro Histórico, Ciudad de Mexico

source_links.title: Food & Pleasure - taquerías a las que sí van los mexicanos

name: Tacos Memo (Mercado San Cosme)
description: Weekday-morning stall inside Mercado San Cosme serving placero tacos with moronga and tártara, and cauliflower tortas.
special_quality: Market-stall tacos with moronga and a vegetarian cauliflower torta.
google_maps_query: Tacos Memo (Mercado San Cosme), San Rafael, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Pozolería San Sebastián
description: Known as 'pozole IMER' for sitting next to the radio station in Xoco. Huge 80-peso bowls with tostadas, cream and lime and a sharp, spicy salsa; finish with tinga or pata tostada.
special_quality: Giant 80-peso pozole bowls beside the IMER radio building.
google_maps_query: Pozolería San Sebastián, Coyoacán, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Pozoles Texcoco
subcategory: Pozole blanco, rojo, verde and mixteco
description: Roma Norte pozolería emphasizing fresh ingredients with white, red, green and Mixtec (hierba santa) versions; Chilango recommends chicharrón, squash blossom and avocado. Average ticket around 250 pesos.
special_quality: One of the few places offering Mixtec-style pozole with hierba santa.
address: Álvaro Obregón 213, Roma Norte (Chilango lists this address; Sopitas gives it for Casa Licha, verify)
google_maps_query: Pozoles Texcoco, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico

name: El Rinconcito de Iguala
description: Fonda with weekday comida corrida known for 10 years for Guerrero-style pozole verde with pork or chicken, avocado and chicharrón, plus chalupas chilpeñas. From about 60 pesos.
special_quality: Guerrero green pozole from a Roma Norte weekday fonda for about 60 pesos.
google_maps_query: El Rinconcito de Iguala, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico

source_links.title: México Desconocido - pozoles verdes estilo Guerrero

name: La Perla Tapatía
description: Family business founded in 1984 in Azcapotzalco serving Jalisco-style birria and white pork pozole with cabbage, onion and radish, red salsa from a secret recipe, cheese and cream shipped from Jalisco. About 190 pesos pp.
special_quality: Jalisco birria and pozole with dairy imported from Jalisco, family-run since 1984.
google_maps_query: La Perla Tapatía, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Birrias Irma Aurora
description: Garibaldi-area birria described by Chilango as authentic Jalisco, with very tender meat steamed in maguey leaf. Limited hours, so verify before going.
special_quality: Birria steamed in maguey leaf, Jalisco style, with short hours.
google_maps_query: Birrias Irma Aurora, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Los Güeros de Juanacatlán
description: Excélsior says it has more than 50 years of tradition near Chapultepec, specializing in quesabirria.
special_quality: Half-century birriería that now leans on quesabirria.
google_maps_query: Los Güeros de Juanacatlán, Ciudad de Mexico
